facts.F360: Layer algebra. Domain: states are pure values; operations are the five translation rules over handed-in data; observation is the set of Domain-namespace types and their IL dependency targets; equality is type full name. Application: operations are the connector port, factories, OAuth and health use cases; observation is the namespace of each type and the IL edges to Adapters, which must be empty; factory interface and class share one namespace; Board and BoardInformation sit beside IBoardInformationProvider. Adapters: connectors, strategies, providers, prober; observation is namespace and that connectors reach no repository. Infrastructure and recovery: unchanged, no timeout, retry, replay or loss behaviour is touched; DI lifetimes and handler order identical.
facts.F361: Checker mapping: placement and dependency-edge claims are decided exactly by the compiled IL through IlDependencies and ModuleRules, each oracle carrying a made-up offender as falsifier; behaviour-free is decided by the existing suites, the live connector suites in CI and the EXAMINE answer comparisons. No Quint, TLA+ or Agda model: there is no state, ordering, concurrency, recovery or liveness claim, and a model would restate the namespace map and could not fail. Quint 0.33.1 is installed (probed with quint --version) and was not run; no waiver is recorded, the formal-model claim set is empty by reason, not by omission. Liveness: not applicable, nothing progresses.
facts.F362: Type and property assessment (object oriented, nw-code-design-oo read): no class is added or changed, so no new anemic type, no Object Calisthenics break and no new invariant owner; each existing rule keeps its cohesive owner. Construction safety: a type cannot silently stay in an old namespace because each layout oracle looks the type up by name in the compiled assembly and fails when it is missing. Property testing: not applicable, every law is a finite list of named types compared both ways, native examples.
facts.F363: Oracle design rule for all four slices: a layout oracle asserts through ModuleRules.TypesLiveInTheirLayer for its layer (and DomainReachesOnlyTheKernelAndTheBaseLibrary in S1), reads types by name from the compiled assembly, fails naming the offender when a type is missing or in the wrong place, and fails when the layer holds no type. An existing rule that finds its subject by namespace or path (SecretCustodySeamArchUnitTest auth pattern, ConnectorPort key, ConnectorRatchetFixtures, ConnectionHealthSingleWriterArchUnitTest, ServiceNow purity tests) proves in the slice that moves its subject that it still names a made-up offender in the new place, or cites TrackerIntegrationRulesSeeTheModuleArchUnitTest. Lists are rewritten to the new names and compared both ways, never loosened. No nWave scenario tags in code.

facts.F365: Risk walk. Stressor: a rule keyed on a path or namespace string goes blind after a move; allowed none, forbidden a vacuous rule; residue owner the slice that moves the subject. Stressor: CI selects live suites by path; A2 already matches both old and new paths, old alternatives stay until feature C. Stressor second set: a Serilog filter or reflection string naming an old category; none found in the repository, a host-side configuration outside it is unknown and accepted. Single point of failure: Program.cs using lines, compile error is immediate. Bypass: reflection or string type names, none found; IL misses catch-clause, event and attribute-named-argument references, covered by the full suite.
